correctness.rationale: PASS: The sum-c edges match all L_i with R_{c−i}; contracting that matching preserves cyclomatic number and yields simple two-distance interval graph H_c(s,t) with s=c−b, t=c−a. Its edges are distances s and t; on Z/(s+t) the translation by s decomposes into g=gcd(s,t) cycles, each with at least three vertices because s<t. Deleting the last g labels (one from each residue class) leaves g paths, so H_{s+t−g−1} is a forest; beyond this cutoff each new vertex remains in its existing residue component, and counting edges 2(N+1)−s−t gives β1=max(0,N+1−s−t+g). Substitution N=c yields the formula and exact strict forest inequality. For any acyclic triple, each added sum d>2c contributes a matching with at most one endpoint in previous nonisolated core; iterating a superlacunary sequence preserves acyclicity. Zeng–Xue–Zeng forest-support theorem then establishes the characteristic-word statement without arbitrary symbol relabeling. Independent original-bipartite-graph union-find verified 12,000 triples, including boundary and gcd cases; analytic graph argument proves all triples.

final_claim: For every 0<=a<b<c, the additive bipartite incidence graph of sums {a,b,c} has cycle rank β1=max(0,a+b−c+gcd(b−a,c−b)+1); it is a forest exactly when c−b>a+gcd(b−a,c−b), precisely characterizing admissible designated sparse-support first-three positions of an infinite Abelian pattern Sturmian characteristic word.
